    - Brindle, captain of the Watch. Which sounds grander than it is: we are a handful of volunteers and a gate. You look like you can handle yourself, *Player*. That makes you interesting to me.
    - *Player*. Pull up a crate. I will not offer you the good one; that is Knox's, and he has carved his name in it.
    - Dagny is at the gate from sundown. Stand where the light is and let her talk. Then the Outworks.
    - Your count is on the slate, chalked in my best hand. The eyes are the eyes. The lanterns are something else. Lux is working on the something else.
    - The Fallen Tower is waiting, *Player*. Say the word and I will show you the way in. Say it when you mean it.
    - Every lantern on the outer wall, lit, three weeks running. I had to rub out a whole column of the slate. I nearly enjoyed it.
    - Low Grad. A whole buried city under our feet, and we posted a guard on the wrong door for a hundred years. I am trying to find that funny.
    - The Table is arguing about the iron door. It will argue all night; that is what it is for. I would rather it argued all night than one of us decided before breakfast.
    - Two doors now. The gate up here and Ferro's grate out in the hillside. I check them both twice. Knox says I check the grate three times. Knox is right.
    - *Player*. The outer wall is lit and the tunnel mouth is barred. Do you know how long it has been since I could say two good things in a row? Sit down before I think of a third.
    - What do you need?
        - *Choice:* Take me into the Fallen Tower.
        - *Choice:* What does the Watch do?
        - *Choice:* What is on the slate?
        - *Choice:* What about Dagny?
        - *Choice:* You and the Open Table?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - Down the side path, into the Outworks, east under the walls till the tower lies on its side. The vault is flooded and open to the sky. Make noise. Come back.
    - When I joined, seventeen years ago, the Watch greeted late carts and settled quarrels over tolls nobody paid. I signed up for one summer, for something to do. I was meant to make rope. Rope is very quiet.
    - Now we stand between the city and whatever comes up the road, which is more every year. Knox knows every face. Dagny keeps the night. I keep the slate and ask the Table for help. Mostly it cheers and goes home.
    - Every sighting the Watch hears of, every week, chalked by road. Walkers' Road, Stonefang Pass, the Outworks. Tick reads it aloud every week, slowly, with feeling. The numbers only go one way.
    - Gloomeyes by the gate road, counted properly now. And under it, in a different chalk: lanterns smashed, outer wall, every second night. Two columns. Two different things. I would like one of them to go away.
    - The lantern column is empty. I left the chalk line under it, so nobody forgets it was ever full. The other columns still go one way. But one is empty, and I look at it every morning.
    - Dagny Roe. Came inland from Bain Harbour to haul lamp oil and put her hand up at the Table when I asked for volunteers. I gave her the night watch because nobody else wanted it.
    - She says she talks to the dark because she is too frightened to do anything else. I have watched her do it for two years. I have a word for what she does out there, and it is not frightened.
    - I have not said it to her. When I do, I want it to land, not scare her off the gate. So I am waiting for the right moment. And checking twice. Knox gives her owls in the meantime.
    - Rook is a friend, and the Table is the best thing this city has, and I stand up at it every month and ask for twenty volunteers. People listen. People nod. Bastian ends his speeches with my call for volunteers now, which is kind and very loud.
    - Then they go back to their workshops. I do not blame them; the Walkers were painters and players, not soldiers. I just wonder what happens the night something gets past the gate before we have decided whose turn it is.
    - Walk safe, *Player*. And check twice.
